newsitem.title: UK: BA vows to fly on despite strike vote.
newsitem.headline: BA vows to fly on despite strike vote.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday a cabin crew vote for strike action was regrettable but vowed to continue to fly and maintain services.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) said an overwhelming majority of cabin crew had voted for a strike and it would decide its next move on Monday.
BA noted it had already agreed a wages package with its other union, Cabin Crew 89, which represents a quarter of mainline cabin staff.
But it criticised the T&G, which represents 9,000 cabin crew, saying it had sold its members short with the strike ballot.

"How do you reach agreement with a union that walks away from the table, particularly when the other union has voted overwhelmingly 'yes'? The outcome of this ballot is regrettable especially as the deal is good for staff," BA chief executive Bob Ayling said in a statement.

BA said its European and domestic services from London's Gatwick airport and services operating by British Airways Regional from the UK regions were not involved in the ballot. Also, staff in its franchise and alliance partners were not part of the vote, BA said.

BA has said would offer employment to others to replace employees who were on strike, a contingency plan slammed by union representatives as creating a "scab army". The T&G predicted services would suffer if new personnel were drafted in.

BA agreed a deal with Cabin Crew 89 comprising a basic wage rise of between 14.2 percent and 24 percent, with higher pensionable salaries and better profit-sharing terms, sickness and maternity leave benefits.
BA said cabin crew would not be any worse off under the new pay restructuring agreement, which is part of the carrier's drive to boost efficiency.
The airline faces a further ballot next Tuesday when 9,000 ground staff vote on plans to sell off BA's catering unit, which employs 1,200 people.
